articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Drops New Nudity-Filled Gameplay, Polls People on Whether to Release Story Spoilers
articles.author: Tom Phillips
articles.content:
The past week's extraordinary set of GTA 6 leaks appear to have continued today with a significant new release of footage that depicts mass nudity. Meanwhile, the leaker has suggested story spoilers could be posted next, and has called on fans to protest outside the offices of Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive.
Today's newly-posted footage from the 'CyberLeek' person or group depicts GTA 6 main character Jason exploring a "nudist town" area filled with naked characters. Male and female genitalia are both fully exposed. Explicit dialogue can be heard as the NPCs party, while the player uses binoculars to zoom in on character models. This action eventually results in a fight breaking out, leading to the player ultimately gunning numerous civilians down.
While the amount of nudity on screen is surprising, the footage is perhaps even more notable for its watermarked message, which claims that footage of a "Lucia-led prologue" could be released next. Once again, the leaker calls for fans to vote on what they should release — cast by spending cryptocurrency that earns the leaker(s) money, it's important to note, something that is widely believed to be a crypto scheme.
Bizarrely, the leaker also calls for a physical show of support from those watching, and states that they want "gamers" dressed up as leeks to hold up game discs while standing outside Rockstar offices in protest.
This marks another significant escalation by those responsible for the leaks, who have called for real-world action for the first time. Additionally, it's worth stating that the gameplay released to date has included two snippets of cutscenes that feature no significant story details, and mostly focus on open-world gameplay of Jason. It seems far more significant footage of the game may leak next.
The leaker also seems to be attempting to highlight their initially-stated reason for the leaks, as a form of protest against the decision not to offer GTA 6 via a physical disc, something that was announced just days before PlayStation revealed it would kill PS5 game discs for new games released from January 2028 onwards.
All of this comes just ahead of Netflix's exclusive "reveal" of GTA 6 gameplay footage via its Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look, which is set for Thursday, August 27, and will remain exclusive on the streaming platform for six hours before it makes its way to other platforms such as YouTube.
According to Bloomberg, Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff. Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks.
GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Take-Two has subpoenaed Microsoft, Discord, and even X / Twitter, but the leaker appears undeterred. IGN has asked Take-Two and Rockstar for comment.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
articles.summary:
New footage from the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 has leaked online, featuring explicit content and threats from the leaker to release further story spoilers and character details.

### Key Points
- The leaked footage depicts the protagonist Jason exploring a nudist town, featuring explicit character models and violent gameplay sequences.
- The leaker, known as "CyberLeek," is soliciting cryptocurrency payments from fans to determine which game assets to release next.
- Protesters are being encouraged to gather outside Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive offices while dressed as leeks to protest digital-only game releases.
- Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive have issued subpoenas to platforms including Discord, Microsoft, and X to identify the source of the leaks.
- Netflix is scheduled to host an exclusive reveal of GTA 6 gameplay footage on August 27, ahead of the game's November 19, 2026, release date.

### Why it Matters
These persistent security breaches create significant internal pressure at Rockstar Games as the studio prepares for its highly anticipated title launch. The situation highlights growing concerns regarding intellectual property protection and the potential for bad actors to exploit fan anticipation for financial gain.

articles.title: The software engineering hiring rebound has a catch: It's leaving early-career engineers behind
articles.author: Jacob Zinkula
articles.content:
After years of layoffs, businesses are hiring more software engineers — but the rebound is spread unevenly.
As of the first quarter of this year, nearly 70% of US software development job postings on Indeed were for senior-level roles, rather than mid- or entry-level. That's up from 55% in early 2019.
Of the more than 40 employment sectors that Indeed analyzed across the economy, software development had the highest share of senior-level postings.
As AI reshapes the economy, software engineering has become a closely watched test case for what the technology could mean for workers. After surging during the early pandemic years, software development job postings began to plummet in 2022. The downturn overlapped with the release of ChatGPT and other AI models, raising questions about whether AI was reducing demand for software engineers.
But over the past year and a half, the trend has started to reverse. Software development postings remain below pre-pandemic levels, but were up roughly 15% in June from early 2025.
In Indeed's analysis, senior engineers appear to be finding their footing in the age of AI, while less-experienced engineers aren't seeing the same recovery.
AI could be giving senior engineers an edge
Sneha Puri, economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said the recent rebound in software development postings has been tied in part to a return to more normal hiring levels in the tech sector after years of slower hiring.
But she said perhaps the likeliest explanation for the uptick is that companies still need people to direct AI tools and review the code they churn out, especially for more complex projects. That need tends to favor senior engineers.
"AI tools can increasingly handle the routine, well-defined coding tasks that used to be assigned to junior engineers," she said. "That shifts hiring demand toward workers who can direct AI output, catch its mistakes, and make the judgment calls AI can't — skills that typically come with experience."
Some software engineers say they've seen that shift firsthand.
Manoj Aggarwal, a software engineer with more than a decade of experience, said he noticed more openings for senior engineering roles than junior ones during a job search last year. In his current role, Aggarwal said AI has transformed his workflow, with much of his coding time now spent prompting AI tools and reviewing their output.
"I think companies will continue to rely on experienced engineers working with AI tools," he said. "That's one reason I'm making sure I stay up to date with those tools."
The pipeline for future senior engineers could be shrinking
The challenges facing early-career engineers aren't entirely new. Puri said that even before the AI boom, software development had a relatively small share of entry-level postings, in part because of the sector's advanced technical requirements.
Indeed is more likely to classify roles as mid-level when employers seek qualifications beyond the typical baseline — in the case of software development, that's a bachelor's degree. These added qualifications, which can include specialized skills, an advanced degree, or prior experience such as internships, have long been common in software development postings.
Software development jobs classified as mid-level haven't necessarily been out of reach for early-career workers. But with the share of mid-level postings falling considerably in recent years, there may be fewer paths for them into the field.
That could pose a challenge not just for early-career engineers, but for employers down the road, Puri said, even if they can get by with fewer junior engineers in the short term.
"Today's entry-level workforce becomes tomorrow's senior-level experts," she said, "and if employers want senior talent capable of managing AI down the line, they need to keep investing in junior talent through entry-level roles now."

articles.summary:
Software engineering job postings are rebounding, but hiring demand is increasingly concentrated on senior-level roles as companies prioritize experienced workers capable of managing and reviewing AI-generated code.

### Key Points
- Nearly 70% of US software development job postings on Indeed in early 2025 were for senior-level roles, compared to 55% in 2019.
- Software development job postings rose approximately 15% in June 2025 compared to early 2024, though they remain below pre-pandemic levels.
- AI tools are increasingly automating routine coding tasks, leading companies to favor engineers who can direct AI output and perform complex quality control.
- The decline in entry-level and mid-level job postings may create a long-term talent gap by limiting the pipeline of workers gaining necessary experience.

### Why it Matters
The shift toward senior-only hiring suggests that AI is fundamentally altering the career trajectory for software engineers by automating entry-level responsibilities. If companies fail to invest in junior talent, they risk a future shortage of experienced professionals capable of overseeing increasingly complex AI-driven development workflows.

articles.title: Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over their rental listings partnership
articles.author: Stevie Bonifield
articles.content:
The FTC and Zillow have announced a settlement that ends the case alleging that a 2025 “partnership” between Zillow and Redfin violated antitrust laws. The FTC had alleged Zillow agreed to pay Redfin to syndicate its listings, while Redfin would end its own advertising contracts and promise not to compete with Zillow for multifamily listings.
Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over their rental listings partnership
They had allegedly conspired to reduce competition in rental listings, leaving fewer options and higher prices.
The FTC’s settlement proposal allows Redfin to continue syndicating rental listings from Zillow “unencumbered by the anticompetitive restraints” in the original deal, but also requires Redfin to restart its own rental listings advertising business, which it wound down as part of the partnership.
Daniel Guarnera, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Competition, said the deal “delivers better, quicker, more certain results for both renters and property management companies than we would have been able to achieve after prevailing at trial.” The state attorneys general of Arizona, Connecticut, New York, Virginia and Washington also agreed to the proposed settlement.
This ending also follows other recent settlements from the Trump administration in high-profile cases of companies behaving badly, like the Live Nation-Ticketmaster case, and its case against Realpage.
articles.summary:
Zillow and Redfin have reached a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission to resolve antitrust allegations regarding a 2025 partnership that restricted competition in the rental listings market.

### Key Points
- The FTC alleged the companies conspired to limit rental listing competition, resulting in fewer consumer options and higher prices.
- Under the settlement, Redfin must resume its independent rental listings advertising business, which was previously wound down under the partnership.
- Redfin is now permitted to syndicate Zillow’s rental listings without the anticompetitive constraints included in the original agreement.
- Attorneys general from Arizona, Connecticut, New York, Virginia, and Washington joined the FTC in approving the proposed settlement.
- This resolution follows a series of recent high-profile antitrust enforcement actions against major corporations, including Live Nation-Ticketmaster and RealPage.

### Why it Matters
This settlement restores competitive pressure in the rental advertising market, potentially lowering costs and increasing choices for both renters and property management firms. By forcing Redfin to restart its advertising business, the FTC aims to prevent market consolidation and ensure that major real estate platforms remain independent competitors.

articles.title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra looks like an outright iPhone copy in this latest leak
articles.author: sanujb6@gmail.com (Sanuj Bhatia) , Sanuj Bhatia
articles.content:
What you need to know
- Early Galaxy S27 Ultra leaks point to a major redesign with a horizontal camera plateau similar to the iPhone 17 Pro.
- Samsung could finally bring native Qi2 support to the Galaxy S27 Ultra, with magnets seemingly visible in leaked renders.
- The Galaxy S27 Ultra could reportedly launch in two sizes, potentially giving buyers a smaller Ultra option for the first time.
With the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series out of the way, attention is now turning toward Samsung's next flagship smartphone lineup. And if the latest round of leaks is anything to go by, the Galaxy S27 Ultra could be getting a major redesign that looks a lot like Apple's latest iPhones.
For the past few years, Samsung has stuck with a vertical camera layout across its Galaxy S lineup. In fact, the company has been criticized several times for shipping very similar-looking Galaxy S Ultra phones year after year. It now looks like Samsung is finally planning to move away from that design, but perhaps not in the direction everyone expected.
Leakers Sonny Dickson, Max Jambor, and Ice Universe have shared what is claimed to be the Galaxy S27 Ultra's new design on X, and it's hard not to see the resemblance to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro lineup.
The leaked design shows a horizontal camera plateau across the back, similar to the latest iPhones, with two large camera rings and an elongated section that will likely house the remaining cameras and LED flash.
It's pretty clear where Samsung may be taking some design inspiration from this time around. On the bright side, though, the leaked renders also appear to show a Qi2 magnetic ring on the back, suggesting Samsung could finally build native Qi2 support directly into the Galaxy S27 Ultra.
The leaks also suggest Samsung could offer the Galaxy S27 Ultra in two different sizes, something we've heard rumored previously. If true, that could mean we're finally getting a more compact version of Samsung's Ultra flagship alongside the larger model.
Of course, we're still months away from the Galaxy S27 series launch, and plenty could change before Samsung makes anything official. But these early leaks certainly suggest Samsung is preparing a pretty major design shake-up, even if the inspiration appears to be coming straight from Cupertino.

articles.title: Apollo blames social engineering for a four-day breach in July
articles.author: Ana Maria Constantin
articles.content:
Apollo Global Management has told people that hackers reached their names, dates of birth, contact details, home addresses and Social Security numbers. The private equity firm set out the incident in a notification letter dated 21 August and posted on the California attorney general’s website.
The letter opens the account of what happened with a comparison. “Similar to other financial services firms, Apollo recently experienced a social engineering incident.”
The dates in the letter
Apollo says there was unauthorised access to certain cloud platforms between 6 and 10 July. That is four days.
The firm then gives a second date. “During our investigation, we learned on August 12, 2026 that the information potentially impacted by this incident included your name, date of birth, contact information, home address, and your Social Security Number.”
The letter went out on 21 August. Six weeks separate the start of the access from the notice.
What Apollo says it did
“Upon detecting the incident, we promptly notified law enforcement, engaged leading outside cybersecurity and forensic experts, enhanced our security protocols, and launched an investigation,” wrote Matthew Breitfelder, Apollo’s global head of human capital.
A line further down the letter addresses California and Wyoming residents. It reads: “This notification was not delayed by law enforcement.”
What the letter does not say
It does not name the attacker. It does not say how many people received it. It does not say who they are, whether staff at Apollo, staff at companies Apollo owns, or investors.
It names no cloud platform, and it does not describe how the attackers got in beyond the phrase “social engineering incident”. Apollo declined to comment to Bloomberg. A spokesperson did not answer TechCrunch’s questions, including whether the firm paid a ransom.
Nor does the list of stolen data include payment details. The categories Apollo names stop at identity information, and no bank or card data appears among them.
The document on the file
What Apollo filed in California is the blank version of the letter. The name field reads “Dear :” and the enrolment code is missing. A print marker sits above the address block.
The file is called L01 Template_CA.pdf. It is the mail-merge master rather than any individual’s copy, which is standard practice for these filings.
Who is sending the letter
The return address is not Apollo’s. Letters go out from “Apollo c/o Cyberscout, P.O. Box 3826, Suwanee, GA 30024”, while the letterhead carries Apollo’s address at 9 West 57th Street in New York.
Cyberscout is providing the credit monitoring. The letter describes it as “a TransUnion company specializing in fraud assistance and remediation services”. TransUnion is one of the three credit bureaus the same letter tells recipients to contact.
The terms of the monitoring offer
The services run for twenty-four months from the date of enrolment, not from the date of the breach. Recipients have 90 days from the letter to enrol.
Enrolment needs an internet connection and an email account. The letter notes it “may not be available to minors under the age of 18 years of age”. A help line runs for 90 days, 8am to 8pm Eastern, weekdays only.
Which states got the letter
The version filed in California carries notices for residents of seven jurisdictions. They are California, the District of Columbia, Maryland, New York, North Carolina, Rhode Island and Wyoming.
Rhode Island residents are told they have the right to obtain any police report filed about the incident.
The campaign around it
Google warned in July that a group it tracks as UNC6671, also called BlackFile, was targeting private equity and financial firms. Reuters reported that Apollo was among the companies targeted, alongside Blackstone, Bridgewater and Bain Capital, without establishing whether any attack had succeeded.
Apollo has not attributed its breach to that group. The Register notes that the notification links the incident to attacks elsewhere without naming anyone.
Google says the group calls employees while posing as colleagues or IT support, then steers them to spoofed login pages that harvest passwords and multi-factor codes. It puts some ransom payments at $750,000. The desk covered the phone-call campaign on 7 August.
The same method elsewhere this month
Levi Strauss said social engineers compromised three employees’ company-issued computers and took corporate data. The desk covered the Levi’s breach on 10 August.
RingCentral lost 1.6 million records after a phone call. The desk covered that leak on 15 August. Point72 told investors it had been attacked. Hackers also tried Millennium Management, Two Sigma and Citadel, according to Bloomberg.
How big Apollo is
TechCrunch puts Apollo’s assets under management at $938bn. The Register describes the firm as a $1tn investment giant. Apollo’s regulatory filings put its headcount at around 5,000 as of February 2026.
TechCrunch disclosed its own connection in its report. Until 2025 it was a subsidiary of Yahoo, an advertising technology company owned by Apollo.
The firm has appeared on this desk twice in three months for reasons unrelated to security. Its economists published research on AI and wages two days ago, which the desk covered as Apollo on paychecks. In May it worked with Blackstone on a $36bn debt deal to buy Anthropic chips.
What Apollo tells recipients to do
The letter asks people to review account statements, monitor credit reports, and consider a fraud alert or a security freeze. It reproduces contact details for Equifax, Experian and TransUnion.
It closes on the state of the inquiry. “Our investigation remains ongoing, and you may receive additional updates from us.”
What has not happened yet
No group has claimed the attack. TechRadar reported at the time of writing that the data had not surfaced on any leak site.
Apollo says the same in its own words. “We have no evidence that your information has been publicly posted or used for identity theft or fraud at this time.”

**Private equity firm Apollo Global Management has notified individuals that hackers accessed sensitive personal information, including Social Security numbers, following a social engineering incident in early July.**

### Key Points
- Unauthorized access to Apollo cloud platforms occurred between July 6 and July 10, 2026.
- Stolen data includes names, dates of birth, contact details, home addresses, and Social Security numbers.
- Apollo is offering affected individuals 24 months of credit monitoring services through Cyberscout, a TransUnion company.
- The breach impacts residents in seven jurisdictions, including California, New York, and the District of Columbia.
- No specific threat actor has claimed responsibility, and Apollo reports no evidence of the stolen data being misused for fraud yet.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the growing vulnerability of major financial institutions to sophisticated social engineering attacks that bypass traditional security protocols. As firms like Apollo manage nearly $1 trillion in assets, such breaches underscore the significant risks posed to the personal data of employees and investors alike.

articles.title: 3 Digital Strategies Small Business Owners Can Use to Do More With Less
articles.author: Sharon Miller
articles.content:
Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
Key Takeaways
- When evaluating digital tools, small business owners can start by organizing their priorities around three goals: efficiency, reach and customer engagement.
- Digital tools can help small business owners improve the customer experience at every touchpoint. And built-in analytics help owners understand what resonates and adjust spending in real time.
- Build a culture of innovation. Rather than adopting tools reactively, a digital road map can help owners take a more intentional approach.
The United States has over 36 million small businesses, and most owners will tell you the work is not easy, but it is fulfilling. Small businesses contribute to 43.5% of the U.S. GDP and employ more than 62 million people, according to the Small Business Administration. Yet these owners face a persistent challenge: pressure to grow with limited resources to do so.
While larger companies can more easily invest in operational systems for accounting, HR, IT and marketing, small businesses often rely on lean teams to manage operations, reach customers, balance the books and strategize for the future.
Technology is changing what is possible for small businesses. Bank of America Institute data shows small businesses have increased their spending on tech services, including artificial intelligence tools. That said, spending more does not always mean spending better, and the challenge lies in identifying which tools will drive growth and then putting them to good use.
Here are three strategies small business owners can use to do exactly that.
1. Prioritize efficiency, reach and engagement
With thousands of digital tools on the market, many owners find it difficult to know if they are making the right choices. When evaluating tools, they can start by organizing their priorities around three goals: efficiency, reach and customer engagement.
Efficiency: Some of the most immediate gains from digital tools show up in efficiency, with early AI adopters citing improvements in productivity and operational efficiency, according to a U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation/Hiring Our Heroes whitepaper. But AI is just one piece of the puzzle.
Project management platforms, scheduling tools and payment processing software can all eliminate many of the manual steps that slow teams down. Accounting and financial management platforms can automate inventory tracking, invoicing and demand forecasting, while customer relationship management (CRM) software can generate follow-ups and surface data-backed insights that inform smarter decision-making.
Reach: Tools like ecommerce platforms and advertising services enable small businesses to sell far beyond their locale and target customers on a national or even global scale. Plus, the data needed to optimize these efforts is often built into the ecommerce, CRM and email marketing platforms many businesses already use. In this way, business owners can not only expand their reach, but gain a clearer picture of what is working, who is buying and where to focus next.
Engagement: Beyond delivering quality products or services, today’s businesses often thrive when they make their customers feel known. Email marketing platforms, loyalty programs and personalized website content can go a long way in driving long-term loyalty. Product recommendation engines, which suggest relevant items based on a customer’s browsing history or past purchases, can enable easier product discovery. Chatbots, whether AI-powered or not, can provide faster support when something goes wrong.
2. Elevate the customer experience
The customer experience is more multifaceted than ever, happening across channels: on a brand’s website, on social media or in a brick-and-mortar store. According to a 2026 survey, 93% of shoppers report that they are more likely to continue shopping with a brand when it gets personalization right, making this a key priority for small businesses looking to build lasting customer relationships.
Digital tools can help small business owners deliver on this at every touchpoint. Social media advertising platforms, for example, enable targeted campaigns that reach new customer segments. In fact, 83% of marketers are confident in social media advertising’s return on investment (ROI), per a 2026 Hootsuite report, making it an investment worth considering.
Built-in analytics help owners understand what resonates and adjust spending in real time. Beyond attracting new customers, tools that support seamless checkout and automate post-purchase follow-up can help sustain a business.
3. Foster a culture of innovation
Small businesses can face greater challenges when evaluating, adopting and using emerging technologies, often due to hurdles like uncertainty about ROI, cybersecurity concerns and workforce resistance. When resources are limited, the pressure to keep up with a fast-moving pace of technological change can feel daunting, yet the urgency is real: The same U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation/Hiring Our Heroes whitepaper found that 53% of small business leaders say AI is either already critical to their operations or will be very soon.
Rather than adopting tools reactively, a digital road map can help owners take a more intentional approach, providing a structured plan for evaluating and implementing technology aligned with their business goals. It should define what success looks like and prioritize initiatives that deliver visible returns, such as automating invoicing and payment reminders to free up time for higher-value work.
Sustaining innovation requires more than the right tools. According to a Google/Ipsos poll, 40% of employees use AI at work, but only 5% are “AI fluent,” meaning they redesign their workflows around AI and regularly apply it. For owners facing this gap, investing in AI education may be a key pillar of their digital road map. Owners who invest in helping employees move from passive AI users to confident, capable ones will compound their return on technology investments.
The digital tools available give small businesses the ability to compete in ways that were once out of reach. By focusing on the right tools, delivering standout customer experiences and building a culture of innovation, owners can create a foundation for lasting growth. The path to getting there does not require an overnight overhaul. It requires a clear plan, a commitment to learning and a willingness to start. For small business owners ready to take that step, the opportunity has never been greater.
Key Takeaways
- When evaluating digital tools, small business owners can start by organizing their priorities around three goals: efficiency, reach and customer engagement.
- Digital tools can help small business owners improve the customer experience at every touchpoint. And built-in analytics help owners understand what resonates and adjust spending in real time.
- Build a culture of innovation. Rather than adopting tools reactively, a digital road map can help owners take a more intentional approach.
The United States has over 36 million small businesses, and most owners will tell you the work is not easy, but it is fulfilling. Small businesses contribute to 43.5% of the U.S. GDP and employ more than 62 million people, according to the Small Business Administration. Yet these owners face a persistent challenge: pressure to grow with limited resources to do so.
While larger companies can more easily invest in operational systems for accounting, HR, IT and marketing, small businesses often rely on lean teams to manage operations, reach customers, balance the books and strategize for the future.
Technology is changing what is possible for small businesses. Bank of America Institute data shows small businesses have increased their spending on tech services, including artificial intelligence tools. That said, spending more does not always mean spending better, and the challenge lies in identifying which tools will drive growth and then putting them to good use.

Small business owners can drive sustainable growth by strategically adopting digital tools to improve operational efficiency, expand market reach, and enhance customer engagement through data-backed personalization.

### Key Points
- Small businesses contribute 43.5% of the U.S. GDP and employ over 62 million people, yet often struggle to scale with limited operational resources.
- Owners should prioritize digital investments that automate manual tasks, such as accounting, inventory tracking, and customer relationship management.
- Data from the Bank of America Institute indicates that small businesses are increasing their spending on technology services, including artificial intelligence.
- A 2026 survey shows that 93% of shoppers are more likely to remain loyal to brands that successfully implement personalized customer experiences.
- Developing a structured digital road map helps businesses move beyond reactive technology adoption toward intentional, goal-oriented growth strategies.
- While 40% of employees use AI at work, only 5% are considered "AI fluent," highlighting the need for owner-led investment in staff education.

### Why it Matters
Strategic technology adoption allows lean small business teams to compete more effectively against larger corporations by optimizing workflows and deepening customer loyalty. By moving from reactive spending to a structured digital road map, owners can maximize their return on investment and ensure long-term operational sustainability.

articles.title: I stopped VPN blocks by turning my home network into a private exit node
articles.author: Afam Onyimadu
articles.content:
When I leave my home, my VPN sometimes fails in a specific way. The streaming services or my banking app that worked well without a VPN start requiring extra authentication, and a few may not load at all. Connection speed stayed good, and tests didn't point to DNS or IP leaks, yet it felt like these sites refused my traffic.
I stopped hitting most of those blocks by dropping the commercial VPN and routing my traffic through a machine at home. The actual problem was the exit IP.
The exit node changed what websites saw
The encryption was never the issue — the exit IP was
Even though I figured the problem was always the VPN, it wasn't easy to confirm. The internet wasn't lagging; the handshake looked fine, and DNS wasn't leaking. The occasional "we can't complete this request now" that I got came with no explanation. When the sites prompt for extra verification, they leave no reason either. For a long time, I felt these sites were reacting to the encryption, but it turned out the problem was the address the traffic originated from.
A service may classify traffic based on the network it belongs to. When you use most commercial VPNs, your traffic is pushed through one of their many servers in data centers, and these sometimes include IP ranges that are cataloged. Even if my connection is clean, it may still be flagged because the service may have been reacting to the reputation or classification of that address; this has nothing to do with connection quality.
What I had to change was to stop exiting through a VPN company's servers; instead, I defaulted to my home network using Tailscale. When I leave my home, the device I carry along communicates to a PC in my home over an encrypted tunnel, which is responsible for sending the traffic to the regular internet, just like it always has. When the site on the other side receives the traffic, it's not looking at it as a VPN provider’s IP. It sees the public IP of my home connection, rather than the VPN provider's exit IP.
Before this switch, the traffic I sent out came from a VPN-provider address, but after this upgrade it came from my home ISP’s block. After the change, the bank apps and streaming platforms that had required extra verification recognized me at once.
My home PC became my VPN exit
One command turned it into the internet-facing end of my connection
Tailscale was already running on my home machine and the devices I take with me. For the longest time, I believed this automatically meant traffic was moving through my home device. I was wrong, because having Tailscale on my devices only created a private network between them. You need to enable the exit node; otherwise, devices won't automatically send traffic through your home connection.
It was, however, a far smaller change than I expected. I first ran this command on my home device:
tailscale up --advertise-exit-node
Next, I opened the admin console and approved it as an exit node. Then I opened the app for the devices that I travel with and picked my home device as the exit node. This simple process didn't require a router change or any of the complex processes I had anticipated. With my home machine acting as an exit node, traffic from the traveling device could route through my home device before reaching the public internet.
Once, while on a network with a strict firewall, I noticed considerable lag when the link stopped going directly and fell back to a relay. But the lag disappeared when I returned to a normal network. It's been a few weeks since I started using this, and I've always been able to reach my home network whenever I need it.
Then my home connection became part of the deal
A residential IP fixes reputation, not everything else
I'm not selling this as a way of becoming invisible. There are other elements like account history, the device itself, typing and click patterns, and location signals that a site may still look at. It wouldn't fix blocks unrelated to IP reputation.
There's also a bandwidth tradeoff. This setup requires traffic to move to the home connection first before going out, which changes how fast things feel from your current network to whatever ceiling the home connection sets. Also, if the home device is asleep or unplugged, you lose your exit node.
Tailscale prefers a direct connection between the devices. When the two endpoints can't establish one, traffic can be relayed through Tailscale's DERP servers instead. That can add latency and reduce throughput, which I noticed on one restrictive network. Many home connections are behind carrier-grade NAT. This wouldn't automatically kill a direct link, but it makes relays more likely, which is where speed drops often occur.
|  | Commercial VPN | Home Tailscale exit node | 
|---|---|---|
| Exit IP | VPN provider’s network | Your home ISP | 
| Setup | Almost none | One-time configuration | 
| Ongoing cost | Usually a subscription | None beyond what you already pay for internet | 
| Performance | Depends on the VPN server | Depends on your home connection | 
| Best fit | General VPN use | Making your traffic look like it’s coming from home | 
The whole trick, and the whole limit
In the end, I didn't make my VPN undetectable, but that wasn't the idea in the first place. All I did was move my exit point away from a VPN provider's address space and back to my residential connection. That removed one particular source of suspicion, but nothing more.
articles.summary:
Users can bypass website blocks and extra authentication prompts by configuring a Tailscale exit node to route internet traffic through their home residential IP address instead of commercial VPNs.

### Key Points
- Commercial VPNs often trigger security blocks because websites flag their data center IP addresses as suspicious or untrusted.
- Routing traffic through a home PC using Tailscale allows users to appear as if they are browsing from their own residential ISP connection.
- Enabling an exit node requires running the command `tailscale up --advertise-exit-node` on a home machine and approving it in the admin console.
- This method relies on the home device remaining powered on and connected to the internet to function as a gateway.
- Performance is limited by the user's home upload bandwidth and potential latency if the connection is forced through Tailscale's relay servers.

### Why it Matters
Using a residential IP address helps users avoid the automated security friction and service denials frequently associated with commercial VPN exit nodes. This approach provides a more reliable way to access banking and streaming services while traveling without sacrificing the security of an encrypted tunnel.

articles.title: Take Five: Six months of war
articles.author: Reuters
articles.content:
Aug 21 (Reuters) - The world's top central bank chiefs gather in Jackson Hole this week against a jittery backdrop, half a year into the Iran war and with bond markets rattled by a selloff in long-dated U.S. debt that prompted U.S. Treasury intervention.
Away from Wyoming, there's plenty else going on, from inflation readings around the world and Nvidia's earnings to a South Korean rate decision and an Icelandic vote on whether to revive EU accession talks.
Here's all you need to know about the week ahead in financial markets, by Howard Schneider in Washington, Laura Matthews in New York, Stine Jacobsen in Copenhagen, Gregor Stuart Hunter in Singapore and Samuel Indyk in London.
1/ GOING FISHING
Big-think or red meat? That's the choice Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh faces as he prepares a keynote address at the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium in Wyoming: expound on his ideas for reforming the central bank, or stick to the nuts and bolts of monetary policy and whether rates are headed higher.
As the gathering kicks off on Thursday, bringing together central bank chiefs from around the world, the audience for his remarks could hardly be more influential.
Warsh has spent his first weeks as chair focusing on long-term structural issues facing the U.S. economy. But investors, still digesting a bond selloff, are craving a steer about the here and now.
Warsh has been pretty clear he doesn't want to show his hand, but he may find his no-guidance policy becoming a liability.
2/ INFLATION WATCH
The prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz and crude prices grinding higher are adding to concerns about the global inflation outlook.
Brent is headed for a second straight weekly gain and its sixth advance in eight weeks, but it's the surge in refined products that is drawing growing attention as the Northern Hemisphere heads towards the colder months.
European diesel prices have jumped more than 70% since the outbreak of war in February; U.S. gasoline is up 60%. With refining output curtailed in the Middle East, Russia, East Asia and beyond, energy-driven inflation looks here to stay.
A clearer picture of global inflation is due in the coming days, with data from Australia on Wednesday, and France, Spain and Tokyo on Friday. Particular focus will fall on the U.S. core PCE reading on Wednesday - expected to print above the Fed's 2% target for the 65th consecutive month.
3/ CHIP CHECK
After a rocky few days for tech stocks, investors will get a fresh read on the artificial intelligence spending boom that has helped propel markets to record highs when Nvidia reports second-quarter results on Wednesday.
articles.summary:
Central bank leaders convene at the Jackson Hole symposium this week as investors seek clarity on monetary policy amid rising global inflation and volatile bond market conditions.

### Key Points
- Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will deliver a keynote address addressing potential central bank reforms and current interest rate trajectories.
- Global energy prices remain elevated, with European diesel and U.S. gasoline costs rising significantly due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
- U.S. core PCE data, expected Wednesday, is projected to remain above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target for the 65th consecutive month.
- Nvidia is scheduled to report second-quarter earnings on Wednesday, providing a critical update on the sustainability of the artificial intelligence spending boom.
- International inflation reports are expected from Australia, France, Spain, and Tokyo throughout the week.

### Why it Matters
These developments highlight the growing tension between long-term structural economic concerns and the immediate pressures of energy-driven inflation. Market participants are closely monitoring these indicators to gauge whether current equity valuations and central bank policies can withstand ongoing geopolitical instability.

articles.title: iPhone 20's Curved Glass Design to Be Made Like iPhone Air
articles.author: Hartley Charlton
articles.content:
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone will be made using the same glass manufacturing process developed for the iPhone Air, according to the leaker known as "Fixed Focus Digital."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said that iPhone Air manufacturing equipment has been modified to produce more rounded glass components for next year's 20th anniversary iPhone, which has helped to reduce Apple's manufacturing costs. The leaker added that overall heat dissipation and thinness have both improved substantially as a result of the changes. 
The claim builds on the leaker's earlier report that a supply chain facility had finished renovations ahead of "iPhone 20" production, with manufacturing quality expected to land somewhere around that of the first-generation iPhone Air. The iPhone Air is Apple's thinnest iPhone to date at 5.6mm and uses a polished titanium frame with a glass back.
The report adds incremental detail to a redesign that has been rumored for well over a year. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple is aiming for a "mostly glass, curved iPhone without any cutouts in the display" to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary, with curved glass wrapping around all sides of the device.
The 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027, following the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 in the spring.
articles.summary:
Apple is reportedly utilizing advanced glass manufacturing processes developed for the iPhone Air to produce a redesigned, curved smartphone model marking the iPhone's 20th anniversary in 2027.

### Key Points
- Apple plans to use modified iPhone Air manufacturing equipment to create rounded glass components for its upcoming 20th-anniversary device.
- The new production process is expected to improve device heat dissipation and overall thinness while simultaneously reducing manufacturing costs.
- Reports suggest the anniversary model will feature a mostly glass, curved design without display cutouts, wrapping glass around all sides of the phone.
- The device is scheduled for a fall 2027 launch, following the release of the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 earlier that year.

### Why it Matters
This manufacturing shift signals Apple's commitment to refining its hardware design language by leveraging existing thin-profile technology for future flagship models. Successfully scaling these complex glass production techniques could set a new standard for durability and aesthetics in the premium smartphone market.

articles.title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
articles.author: Andrew Grush
articles.content:
Chrome's new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
Aug 24, 2026 — 6:30 AM ET
A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities.
Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case. It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.
So, what are your options when it comes to ad-blocking? These days, you won’t find full ad-blocking support on Chrome, but there are still a few solutions for those set on sticking with Google’s popular browser.
With Chrome's latest changes, what is your preferred route for ad-blocking?
AdGuard
The new changes to the Chrome browser make it hard to add truly comprehensive, high-level blocking directly. But what if you didn’t need to in the first place? AdGuard is an app that runs outside your browser and can do much more than just block ads on the sites you use.
Not only can AdGuard block ads in other apps and services beyond the browser, but it can also protect you from trackers, malware, phishing, social widgets, and other security threats. It’s also extremely easy to set up and get started, with a wide range of supported platforms including iOS, Android, Windows, and macOS.
AdGuard is free for just one device, but if you want multi-device coverage, parental controls, and the ability to block ads in apps and games, you’ll need a personal account starting at $2.49 a month. Honestly, in 2026, you won’t find a better option if you need Chrome support and robust blocking that covers malware, tracking, and more.
Please be aware that while you can download this app from Google Play, this version removes Chrome support and makes a few other tweaks. Thankfully, the AdGuard website has an APK you can sideload if you want to keep using Chrome.
uBlock Origin Lite
While uBlock Origin offers deep customization and maximum protection, it’s simply no longer available in Chrome. Thankfully, uBlock Origin Lite is a nice alternative if you want a blocking solution that’s fully compatible with the newer Manifest V3 standard.
The Lite version not only removes custom filter lists and dynamic filtering, but it also lacks an element picker that lets you target stubborn pop-ups, and it offers limited protection against malicious links. If you are just looking to cut out ad clutter and make the web slightly easier to navigate, you’ll find the Lite version is up for the job.
If you are looking for more comprehensive coverage, this isn’t a great option. It ultimately depends on what you’re looking for and what kind of user you are. For a casual web user scrolling social media and streaming videos, this could be a good enough solution without having to look to use an outside app like AdGuard or an alternative browser like Firefox.
Using a Private DNS
As much as I recommend AdGuard for most users, it isn’t without its downsides. First, the app can be a bit bloated and may impact your battery life. It’s also expensive if you want to unlock its full feature potential. A free workaround here is to use Android’s Private DNS features.
While there are many custom DNS options you can configure directly in Android, I highly recommend NextDNS, which is totally free as long as you keep your queries to 300,000 per month. What does that mean exactly? A query is a single DNS lookup request made by a device. Depending on how much you browse, this could be more than enough for most users, but there’s also a Pro option that gives you unlimited access for $1.99 a month or as little as $20 a year.
NextDNS works similarly to AdGuard in its core functionality, meaning it can block ads and trackers and provide a safer web experience for kids and families all at once. Of course, configuring DNS also means you don’t have to install another app on your phone, so the resource impact should be minimal.
Setting up NextDNS is as simple as registering an account on NextDNS’s website; then go to the Setup tab and the Endpoints section. From there, you’ll want to copy or write down your DNS-over-TLS/QUIC hostname (found within your NextDNS account settings). Once you have this, simply go to Settings > Network & Internet > Advanced > Private DNS (exact steps can vary depending on the Android skin and version). Select Private DNS provider hostname and paste in the unique NextDNS hostname you copied. Tap Save, and that’s it.
While this method is built with Android in mind, you can do the same thing directly from the desktop versions of Chrome by clicking on the three-dot menu and going to Settings > Privacy and Security > Security. You’ll then scroll to the Use Secure DNS option, turn it on, and configure it basically the same way.
Consider switching browsers instead
Let’s be honest, Chrome might be a popular browser, but it’s not without its faults. Not only is Google working hard to remove some of the control we once had over the browser, but it’s also a known resource hog — especially on desktop. Now might be the right time to consider another browser.
Brave browser is a natural choice if you’re looking to take privacy and security to the next level. Not only does it have ad-blocking and tracker-blocking features baked in, but it’s also optimized for battery life and highly compatible with Chrome, as it’s built on the same Chromium engine.
Want more power to control things as you see fit? I would highly recommend Firefox if you are looking for something as robust as Chrome and prefer to find your own security solutions. Firefox not only supports the full uBlock Origins experience, but it’s also generally faster than Chrome.
articles.summary:
Google has officially phased out Manifest V2 technology in Chrome, rendering many traditional ad blockers obsolete and forcing users to seek alternative solutions for managing web advertisements.

### Key Points
- Google’s transition to the Manifest V3 standard has made it impossible to use advanced extensions like the original uBlock Origin within the Chrome browser.
- AdGuard offers a robust, system-wide alternative that blocks ads and trackers across apps and browsers, with personal plans starting at $2.49 per month.
- uBlock Origin Lite is a new, Manifest V3-compliant version that provides basic ad-clutter removal but lacks the advanced filtering capabilities of its predecessor.
- Users can configure Private DNS services like NextDNS to block ads at the network level, which minimizes resource usage and works across multiple devices.
- Switching to privacy-focused browsers like Brave or Firefox allows users to retain advanced ad-blocking features that are no longer supported by Chrome.

### Why it Matters
The shift to Manifest V3 significantly limits the ability of browser extensions to intercept and block web traffic, fundamentally changing how users manage their online privacy. This transition forces a trade-off between staying within the Google ecosystem and maintaining the granular control over ad-blocking that many power users require.

articles.title: WordlistLoader Delivers Amatera via ClickFix, SynkLoader Phishes Windows Passwords
articles.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
articles.content:
Cybersecurity researchers have flagged two new malware families called WordlistLoader and SynkLoader that's used to deliver next-stage payloads and likely sell access to ransomware groups.
According to findings from Gen Digital, WordlistLoader is being used to deliver Amatera Stealer (aka ACR Stealer or AcridRain Stealer) via ClearFake campaigns, which employ the ClickFix (aka FakeCaptcha) technique to dupe victims into running malicious commands under the pretext of completing CAPTCHA verification checks.
"Once the visitor clicks on the 'I'm not a robot' checkbox, they're walked through the well-known ClickFix flow, where a malicious command is copied into their clipboard and the victim is instructed to paste it into the Windows Run dialog and execute it, leading to the download of WordlistLoader that ultimately results in the execution of Amatera," security researcher Vojtěch Krejsa said.
The ClickFix prompts are displayed on real websites that have been compromised with malicious JavaScript that's injected in the form of a Base64-encoded blob. The blob, for its part, fetches another JavaScript from a smart contract stored on the blockchain, an approach known as EtherHiding, and dynamically executes the retrieved code. Some of the compromised websites serving ClickFix prompts are below -
- abogadosrosarinos[.]com
- aptisweb[.]com
- avene-hebergement[.]com
- https-xhamster[.]com
- www.caesarjaco.co[.]id
- skybap[.]shop
In recent months, ClearFake campaigns have been revamped to use "cdn.jsdelivr[.]net" to host the threat actor's malicious JavaScript, highlighting the abuse of a legitimate Content Delivery Network (CDN) to stage rogue payloads.
"Although the CDN is meant for hosting JavaScript, the threat actors are actually using it to host their malicious PowerShell script," Expel noted earlier this January. "While jsDelivr appears to be taking down the actor's malicious repositories fairly quickly, the first stage's use of EtherHiding allows them to easily swap out burned URLs for fresh working ones."
The ClickFix command uses "conhost" to launch a hidden "cmd.exe" process, then map a remote WebDAV share using pushd, and finally launch the loader via "rundll32.exe." It's worth noting this WebDAV-based approach overlaps with a similar campaign recently highlighted by Microsoft.
In this campaign, a ClickFix prompt instructs the target to run a command that launches "cmd.exe," which subsequently invokes "rundll32.exe" to load a DLL from a remote WebDAV share accessed over HTTPS. Three different versions of the command have been recorded -
- Direct rundll32 invocation
- pushd-Mounted WebDAV Share followed by rundll32.exe invocation
- Headless and obfuscated pushd execution followed by rundll32.exe invocation (which matches the WordlistLoader infection chain)
"In the more advanced variant, threat actors further enhance stealth by launching commands through conhost.exe –headless, suppressing visible console windows, and employing environment variable obfuscation with delayed variable expansion to conceal critical execution components such as pushd, rundll32, and the remote host name," Microsoft said.
"Combined with minimized or headless execution, these techniques reduce user visibility, complicate static analysis and detection, and enable the infection chain to execute with minimal indication to the victim."
The primary difference is that the Python-based loaders observed by Microsoft between late April 2026 and mid-June 2026 in connection with the ACR Stealer intrusion chain have been replaced by WordlistLoader. ACR Stealer has also been propagated via ClickFix prompts that trigger a command spawning MSHTA to retrieve and execute remote HTA content from a threat actor-controlled domain.
This leads to the execution of a VBScript loader that decodes and runs PowerShell designed to fetch a JPEG image from an image-hosting service and extract it from the stealer payload in memory to minimize on-disk artifacts and complicate detection and analysis.
"The primary purpose of WordlistLoader, an intermediate stage in the Amatera infection chain, is to reconstruct a shellcode that serves as the entry point for subsequent stages," Gen Digital said. At the same time, it employs a hardware-breakpoint-based method to bypass Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) and avoid leaving traces of malicious activity.
WordlistLoader gets its name from the fact that the shellcode is stored in encoded form as a sequence of plain English words, with each word representing one byte. Gen said it also identified a variant that replaces the wordlist with an array of 16-byte UUID-encoded chunks.
The shellcode ultimately makes use of a reflective loader responsible for unpacking and loading Amatera 4.3.3-alpha1. The same reflective loader was observed in late April 2026 in connection with another ClickFix campaign delivering the stealer malware.
The latest version of the stealer comes with updated static obfuscation, hardened syscall invocation through the WoW64 transition, dynamically generated x64 indirect-syscall trampolines invoked through Heaven's Gate, and a redesigned application-bound encryption (ABE) bypass that appears to be directly inspired by Remus Stealer.
SynkLoader Pushed via Microsoft Teams Phishing
The development comes as SynkLoader has been distributed via a Microsoft Teams phishing campaign to siphon a victim's system login credentials by serving a fake lock screen. The activity was detected by Expel in mid-August 2025.
"Someone using a <username>@<company>.onmicrosoft.com email (Microsoft 365's default email domain for companies) reached out to the target using the name IT Service Desk (<Fake Name>)," Expel security researcher Marcus Hutchins said.
"The IT service desk convinced the user to download and install an MSI installer from a Microsoft Azure file storage endpoint (https://filereserve.blob.core.windows[.]net/vgnghuyk/331/331.msi), which gave the file the appearance of having come from Microsoft."
The MSI installer presents itself as a PowerShell Cleaner, which, when run, extracts a ZIP archive and a PowerShell script, the latter of which is automatically run in memory. The script is used to extract the contents of the archive and launch from it a Python-based loader that chooses one of three hard-coded command-and-control (C2) domains and checks in with the server at random, while sleeping for 90 to 120 seconds between requests.
The loader then decrypts and executes the responses from the server. At least seven different modules have been identified -
- System Profiler, a C# DLL to collect data about the target system.
- Persistence Module, a native DLL to create a randomly named scheduled task that launches SynkLoader every time the victim logs into the system and daily at 10 a.m.
- PhishLocker, a DLL to serve a fake Windows lock screen to capture the user's login password
- TrafficRedirector, a backconnect or reverse proxy that allows the attacker to reach the local network services or route internet traffic through the infected machine
- Interactive Shell, a remote access trojan (RAT) module to execute PowerShell commands and transmit the result
- StreamMaster, a Virtual Network Computing (VNC) module to stream the victim's desktop and enable remote mouse and keyboard control
- Status Checker, a Python script to report back the status of which modules are currently running on the system
It's not clear what the end goals of the operator are, but it's suspected that the toolkit may be part of a ransomware group or an initial access broker.
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have identified two new malware families, WordlistLoader and SynkLoader, which are being used to deliver malicious payloads and facilitate unauthorized access for potential ransomware operations.

### Key Points
- WordlistLoader delivers the Amatera Stealer by tricking users into executing malicious commands through deceptive "ClickFix" CAPTCHA verification prompts on compromised websites.
- The WordlistLoader infection chain utilizes hardware breakpoints to bypass Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) and reconstructs shellcode from encoded English word sequences.
- SynkLoader is distributed via Microsoft Teams phishing campaigns, masquerading as an IT service desk to trick victims into installing a malicious MSI file.
- Once installed, SynkLoader deploys various modules, including a fake Windows lock screen to capture credentials, a remote access trojan, and a VNC module for desktop control.
- Threat actors are increasingly abusing legitimate services like jsDelivr CDNs and Azure storage endpoints to host malicious scripts and evade security detection.

### Why it Matters
These sophisticated loaders demonstrate a growing trend of using social engineering and legitimate infrastructure to bypass traditional security defenses. By facilitating initial access and credential theft, these tools provide a critical entry point for ransomware groups to compromise enterprise networks.

articles.title: Gemini Expands Prediction Market Offering
articles.author: Editorial Staff
articles.content:
Cryptocurrency exchange Gemini (NASDAQ: $GEMI
Gemini, founded by the twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, is teaming up with privately held Apex to expand distribution of its prediction markets to brokerage firms.
In a statement, the companies said that Gemini will become the exclusive provider of event contracts distributed by Apex to its brokerage clients.
More From Cryptoprowl:
Gemini will handle execution and clearing, allowing brokerages using Apex to offer crypto-based event contracts without having to build their own connections to a prediction-market exchange.
Prediction markets let people bet on the outcome of real-world events such as sports and elections and have exploded in popularity over the past year.
Sports, politics, and cryptocurrency have emerged as the most popular trades on prediction markets.
The arrangement with Apex has the potential to broaden Gemini’s distribution as it aims to compete for a share of the rapidly growing prediction-market sector.
The leading platforms in the prediction market space remain privately held Kalshi and Polymarket. Gemini is one of several companies trying to break into the space.
Crypto firms such as Gemini are turning to prediction markets in an effort to diversify their revenue streams amid weaker trading volumes.
“We believe that predictions are the future of markets,” said Gemini CEO Tyler Winklevoss in the statement.
GEMI stock has declined 87% since the company went public last September and currently trades at $4.28 U.S. per share.
articles.summary:
Cryptocurrency exchange Gemini has partnered with Apex to become the exclusive provider of event contracts for brokerage firms, aiming to expand its reach within the prediction market sector.

### Key Points
- Gemini will manage execution and clearing for event contracts distributed through Apex’s network of brokerage clients.
- The partnership allows brokerages to offer prediction markets on sports, politics, and cryptocurrency without building independent exchange infrastructure.
- Gemini is entering a competitive market currently dominated by private platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket.
- The move serves as a strategic effort by Gemini to diversify revenue streams following a period of weaker trading volumes.
- Gemini stock has fallen 87% since its public debut last September, currently trading at $4.28 per share.

### Why it Matters
This partnership signals a broader industry shift as crypto exchanges seek to integrate prediction markets into traditional brokerage platforms to capture growing consumer interest. By streamlining access to these speculative assets, Gemini aims to secure a stronger foothold in a competitive sector while attempting to stabilize its financial performance.

articles.title: Google Answers If Some Sites Can Ignore GEO And Just Focus On SEO via @sejournal, @martinibuster
articles.author: Roger Montti
articles.content:
Google’s John Mueller answered a question about industries in which Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) does not matter. His answer showed what it looks like from Google’s point of view.
Generative Engine Optimization And SEO
Businesses have been demanding solutions for ranking in AI-based search and if people are lining up with cash in hand to buy something people are going to sell them what they’re asking for.
Consultants focused on AI search optimization have popped up while established SEOs have reluctantly began offering those services while also affirming that it’s just SEO.
Most SEO plugins now offer the ability to generate LLMs.txt, a file that points LLMs to LLM-optimized markdown content, which no search engine or AI chat actually uses… But the customer is always right.
Industries Where GEO Doesn’t Matter?
Bluesky member @galloni.net asked:
“@johnmu.com, are there industries where GEO simply doesn’t matter yet? I’m thinking about sectors like adult, gambling or other areas where Google still seems to drive most discovery.”
Google’s Mueller answered that from Google’s point of view there is nothing special that needs to be done for AI search.
Mueller responded:
“I’m not quite sure what you’re asking; from our POV there’s nothing really special you need to do for generative AI responses in search.”
Why Nothing Special?
Google’s AI search results derive directly from the crawled index. They pick from the top of the search results for a given query plus additional results for the query fan-outs, which are generally related searches, searches for additional information that a user would be interested in.
Because Google literally pulls AI search results from their regular search index, there is nothing special that businesses and publishers need to do to rank in it beyond regular SEO.
Featured Image by Shutterstock/Lana Leon
articles.summary:
Google Search Advocate John Mueller clarified that businesses do not need specialized strategies for Generative Engine Optimization because AI search results are derived directly from the existing index.

### Key Points
- John Mueller stated that Google’s AI-generated search responses rely on the same crawled index used for traditional search results.
- AI search features pull content from top-ranking pages and related queries, requiring no unique optimization tactics beyond standard SEO practices.
- Many consultants and plugins currently market "Generative Engine Optimization" services, despite Google confirming these specialized efforts are unnecessary for ranking.
- The clarification followed a query regarding whether specific industries, such as gambling or adult content, require distinct approaches for AI-driven discovery.

### Why it Matters
This guidance simplifies the evolving search landscape by confirming that traditional SEO remains the primary driver for visibility in AI-powered search results. Businesses can avoid investing in unproven optimization tools and instead focus on maintaining high-quality, indexable content to ensure performance across all Google search formats.
